title: Quarter runway & mitigation plan to align Private/VPC upgrades with customer migration commitments
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Several enterprise customers on Private/VPC/on-prem plans have signed migration windows tied to regulatory timelines. Our current private upgrade cadence and communication runway are not guaranteed to meet those contractual commitments. This ticket defines a quarter-level runway that coordinates engineering rollout windows, customer communications, rollback/compatibility guardrails, and support staffing to minimize customer disruption.
acceptance_criteria: A documented quarter-long rollout calendar published to stakeholders and customers with >95% clarity on upgrade windows
Compatibility matrix for supported private versions published for release private-2026.06
Canary and rollback playbooks validated in staging and rehearsal with SRE (runbook rehearsal checklist completed)
Agreement on SLA/maintenance window language with legal and CS for customers with migration commitments
milestones: Week 1: Finalize upgrade calendar and gating criteria; PM sign-off
Week 2-3: Eng implements soft gates + compatibility checks; runbook draft
Week 4: Customer comms templates and legal review
Week 8-10: First customer wave with enhanced monitoring
Week 12: Post-wave retro and decision on next quarter cadence
okrs: OKR: Deployment Reliability — reduce private deployment-related incidents by 40% this quarter
OKR: Customer Trust — ensure 100% of customers with migration contracts have documented upgrade commitments
OKR: Operational Efficiency — reduce mean time to rollback for private upgrades to under 30 minutes
risks: Late engineering gating could force unplanned maintenance windows for customers
Compatibility regressions for customer-pinned model versions
Insufficient on-call staffing for coordinated rollouts across timezones
Legal contract language mismatch for maintenance vs. upgrade commitments

notes: Decision: use staged wave approach (internal -> low-risk customers -> high-risk customers) with minimum 72-hour observation period between waves
Trade-off: shorter rollout reduces time-to-value but increases risk of missing regressions. Chosen middle-ground balances 72-hour observation with targeted canaries.
Follow-up: If runtime regressions detected during wave 1, escalate to rollback within defined 30-minute target.
